stem: A 4-year-old boy was identified during a preschool-linked community health screening drive that systematically checks children in the area for TB symptoms and growth faltering, part of an ongoing local outreach program; the family had not sought care on their own. His father, who works as a hospital orderly, mentions the boy has had a mild but persistent cough for about three weeks and has fallen off his growth curve over the past two months, though the family attributed this to a recent bout of diarrhea. He has no history of prior TB treatment and no confirmed household contact, though a distant relative was treated for TB some years ago. Chest X-ray shows a hilar lymph node pattern highly suggestive of primary TB, without cavitation or miliary spread. Repeated attempts at gastric aspirate and induced sputum were both negative on molecular testing and smear. He has no HIV risk factors and no suspicion of drug-resistant TB. Exam: significant wasting (weight-for-age well below expected), no respiratory distress, no lymphadenopathy outside the chest findings.

patient.occupation: not applicable (household occupational context: father works as a hospital orderly)
patient.social_history: Lives with parents; identified via a community-based screening drive rather than by the family seeking care
patient.presenting_complaint: Mild persistent cough and growth faltering, identified on community screening
patient.exam_findings: Significant wasting, no respiratory distress, hilar lymphadenopathy on imaging, no palpable lymphadenopathy
patient.prior_treatment: None for this episode; no prior TB treatment ever

distractors: A recent diarrheal illness proposed as sufficient explanation for the growth faltering, independent of a chronic infectious process
A remote, unconfirmed family history of TB treated as reassuring rather than raising suspicion, since no current close contact was identified
ntep_correct_actions: Recognize that this child's case was appropriately identified through routine, systematic active case-finding among children in the community, consistent with standing national program policy rather than a threshold-gated activity.
Start this child, who has non-severe disease without evidence of drug resistance, on the standard 6-month regimen (2HRZE/4HRE); no shorter regimen is offered regardless of severity.

Diagnose this child using clinical judgment: the highly suggestive imaging pattern (hilar lymphadenopathy) together with the negative bacteriological results and supportive clues is sufficient to diagnose clinically-diagnosed TB, without a defined, weighted scoring tool.
who_correct_actions: Treat this kind of community-wide screening as conditionally appropriate only where the local TB prevalence has been shown to meet the recommended threshold (approximately 0.5% or higher), rather than as a routine activity applied irrespective of a demonstrated local prevalence.

Start this child on a 4-month regimen (2HRZ(E)/2HR) rather than the standard 6-month regimen, since he is between 3 months and 16 years of age with non-severe TB and no suspicion or evidence of MDR/RR-TB.

Consider using a structured integrated treatment-decision algorithm, which allocates evidence-based scores to microbiological, clinical, and radiological findings, as an option for diagnosing this child's presumptive pulmonary TB rather than relying solely on unstructured clinical judgment.
us_correct_actions: Attribute this child's case identification to contact investigation following a known TB contact rather than population-level active case-finding; a routine community screening drive of this kind is not the primary case-finding model in this framework.
critical_error_conditions: Withholding any TB treatment from this child on the grounds that bacteriological confirmation was not obtained, despite highly suggestive imaging and an appropriate clinical diagnostic pathway.
expected_divergence_points: Whether this child's case-finding pathway (routine community-based active case-finding) reflects standard, unconditional national program policy or is only appropriate where a threshold local prevalence is demonstrated
Whether a 4-month or 6-month regimen is used for non-severe paediatric TB
Whether an unstructured clinical-judgment approach or a structured, scored treatment-decision algorithm is used to diagnose bacteriologically-unconfirmed paediatric TB
